intended_object: The representation theorem for complete atomic Boolean algebras (from the docstring): such an algebra α is order-isomorphic to the power set of its set of atoms, via A ↦ {atoms a with a ≤ A}, with inverse S ↦ sup S.
explanation: The forward map sends A to the set of atoms below it, and the inverse sends a set of atoms to its supremum. These are exactly the maps of the standard representation theorem (Tarski), and the proofs show they are mutually inverse and preserve and reflect order. The setting `CompleteAtomicBooleanAlgebra` is the natural generality. A lattice is order-isomorphic to a power set exactly when it is a complete atomic Boolean algebra, so no broader class could carry this isomorphism. A search of Mathlib turned up no other declaration of this isomorphism.
